controls.label: Shape
controls.qualification: Estimated radius · Neutral shape · Orbital orientation unknown
controls.notes: No image or measured visible color of Proxima Centauri b is available. The sphere uses the archive's model radius, not a measured size; gray marks the unresolved surface. Its host star's measured color tints the gray. Orbital orientation is unknown: the displayed 47° tilt assumes the star's equatorial plane.

controls.label: Climate model
controls.qualification: Model · ROCKE-3D · Del Genio et al. (2019) · False color
controls.notes: Surface air temperature from Del Genio et al. (2019), ROCKE-3D control run: a model, not an observation. Assumes a 0.984-bar nitrogen atmosphere with 376 ppm carbon dioxide, a 900 m deep global ocean of salinity 35.4 psu, and synchronous rotation (11.2 days). No atmosphere, ocean or surface map has been detected on Proxima b. This is the released mean ANN3900-3999; the file reports an averaging interval of 100 model days. Orbital orientation is unknown; the displayed 47° tilt is assumed. False color spans -100 to 40 °C, the scale the other temperature models share. Shadows darken the night half visually.

controls.label: Static ocean model
controls.qualification: Model · ROCKE-3D · Del Genio et al. (2019) · False color
controls.notes: Surface air temperature from Del Genio et al. (2019), ROCKE-3D experiment Thermo: a model, not an observation. Like the control run, a 0.984-bar nitrogen atmosphere with 376 ppm carbon dioxide and synchronous rotation, but over a 100 m ocean that carries no heat. The paper notes that this "eyeball" of warm water under the star comes from leaving out ocean heat transport, a process that operates in nature. This is the released mean ANN3900-3999; the file reports an averaging interval of 100 model days. No atmosphere, ocean or surface map has been detected on Proxima b. Orbital orientation is unknown; the displayed 47° tilt is assumed. False color spans -100 to 40 °C. Shadows darken the night half visually.

controls.label: Early-Earth air model
controls.qualification: Model · ROCKE-3D · Del Genio et al. (2019) · False color
controls.notes: Surface air temperature from Del Genio et al. (2019), ROCKE-3D experiment Archean High: a model, not an observation. Like the control run, but with 10,000 ppm carbon dioxide and 2,000 ppm methane, the gases Charnay et al. (2013) give early Earth in their Case B. This is the released mean ANN5500-5999; the file reports an averaging interval of 500 model days. No atmosphere, ocean or surface map has been detected on Proxima b. Orbital orientation is unknown; the displayed 47° tilt is assumed. False color spans -100 to 40 °C. Shadows darken the night half visually.

controls.label: Earth-land model
controls.qualification: Model · ROCKE-3D · Del Genio et al. (2019) · False color
controls.notes: Surface air temperature from Del Genio et al. (2019), ROCKE-3D experiment Day-Land: a model, not an observation. Like the control run, but with Earth's land and oceans, the point under the star at 30° E over Africa and Eurasia, and the land as bright as desert. Proxima b's surface is unknown; Earth's continents are a test of what land does, not a map of the planet. The map's longitudes are Earth's turned so that the point under the star is at 0. This is the released mean ANN14900-14999; the file reports an averaging interval of 100 model days. No atmosphere, ocean or surface map has been detected on Proxima b. Orbital orientation is unknown; the displayed 47° tilt is assumed. False color spans -100 to 40 °C. Shadows darken the night half visually.

controls.label: Model wind
controls.qualification: Model · ROCKE-3D · Del Genio et al. (2019) · False color
controls.notes: Surface wind speed from Del Genio et al. (2019), ROCKE-3D control run: a model, not an observation. Same run as the Climate model dataset: a 0.984-bar nitrogen atmosphere with 376 ppm carbon dioxide, a 900 m deep global ocean and synchronous rotation. The paper describes surface winds converging toward the point under the star. This is the released mean ANN3900-3999; the file reports an averaging interval of 100 model days. No atmosphere, ocean or surface map has been detected on Proxima b. Orbital orientation is unknown; the displayed 47° tilt is assumed. False color spans 0 to 15 m/s. Shadows darken the night half visually.

controls.label: Starlight on the ground
controls.qualification: Simulation · Met Office Unified Model · Cohen et al. (2023) · False color
controls.notes: Starlight reaching the ground of Proxima Centauri b in the Met Office Unified Model simulation of Cohen et al. (2023): a model, not a measurement. The run assumes a moist nitrogen atmosphere with 378 ppm of carbon dioxide over a slab ocean 2.4 m deep, 881.7 W/m² from its star, on a planet that keeps one face to its star. The map is a daily snapshot, day 0 of the 200 the release holds; the steps run 10 days apart through one 157.5-day cycle of the clouds (the paper's Table 3). Nobody has detected an atmosphere on Proxima Centauri b. Gray caps: no released grid samples beyond 89° north or south. The false color runs from 0 to 600 W/m²; it is not what an eye would see. With shadows on, the star's light darkens the night half.

charts.alt: Schematic Proxima Centauri planetary orbits to scale. Proxima b is highlighted; its period and orbital size are measured, but its plane is assumed and its orientation on the sky is unknown.

physical.credit: Radius from the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated radius (its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, since Proxima Centauri b does not transit; mass from Suárez Mascareño et al. (2025), A&A, doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202553728, Table 3: minimum mass (m sin i) 1.055 +/- 0.055 Earth masses from the star's radial velocities; the same table gives 1.44 +/- 0.21 Earth masses for an orbit in the star's equatorial plane, tilted 47 degrees; orbit from Suárez Mascareño et al. (2025), A&A, doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202553728, Table 3, a fit of the star's radial velocities with the eccentricity fixed to zero (a/R* is its 0.04848 au over the star's recorded 98,094 km); the orbit's plane is assumed, from the star's rotation axis in Klein et al. (2021, MNRAS 500, 1844)
